title: deploy() builds a shell command via string interpolation, unlike rollback()
body: subprocess.run(f"kubectl set image deploy/api api={tag}", shell=True, check=True) interpolates tag directly into a string that is then re-parsed by a shell. Any tag containing whitespace, quotes, or shell metacharacters (semicolons, &&, backticks, $(...), pipes) is not passed as the literal value of api=<tag> -- the shell reinterprets it, so the command that actually executes is not the one the caller intended, and it can execute arbitrary additional shell tokens. This is a real correctness defect, not just style: rollback() immediately below does the equivalent operation correctly with an argv list and no shell=True. deploy() should follow the same pattern.

title: New deploy()/rollback() behavior has no test coverage
body: This adds two new functions that shell out to kubectl (deploy() at line 4, rollback() at line 9-10), with no accompanying test that exercises either one -- e.g. by monkeypatching subprocess.run and asserting the constructed argv/command. These are not trivial pass-throughs (deploy() builds a command from user input; rollback() drives a production rollback), so a caller could change the constructed command -- as happened here with the shell=True string form -- without any test failing. At minimum, assert the exact args passed to subprocess.run for both functions.
